candidate_set.description: Frozen gear-norm-v1: Gear table from splitmix64, hash reset per chunk, low b+1/b-1 bit masks (NC-1 equivalent), no cut before minimum, forced maximum
Gear with FastCDC-2020 spread (high-bit) masks at NC-2, same min/max semantics, new chunker_id
Original FastCDC (USENIX ATC 2016): Gear hash with normalized chunking and sub-minimum cut-point skipping, one byte per step; the Phase B2 harness plan lists FastCDC-2016 separately from 2020
Full FastCDC 2020: normalized spread masks, hash skipping before minimum, rolling-two-bytes optimization with identical boundaries
Two Thresholds Two Divisors (Eshghi and Tang 2005): Rabin-based chunking with a backup divisor; the classic literature baseline for chunk-size variance
Rabin polynomial rolling hash over a 48-64 byte window (restic-style), optionally per-archive polynomial
Cyclic-polynomial BuzHash rolling hash (casync, Borg 1.x buzhash, kopia)
Asymmetric Extremum hashless chunking with corrected h~mu-256 parameterization (lowest size variance)
Rapid Asymmetric Maximum hashless chunking (high throughput; pathological on low-entropy data)
SeqCDC hashless monotonic byte-run chunking
VectorCDC/VRAM SIMD hashless chunker with a scalar reference and cross-ISA boundary identity
Chonkers CDC with provable chunk-size and edit-locality bounds (unoptimised reference today)
QuickCDC/RapidCDC-style fast-forwarding that accepts memoized lengths on partial feature-vector matches
Fixed-size blocks (Duplicati, MSIX, Nydus) as measurement baseline

correction_reason: round1 program-code critic: Task 8.1 and the Phase B2 harness plan (ebr-chunk: gear-norm-v1 plus FastCDC-2016/2020, Rabin, BuzHash, AE, RAM, fixed) name FastCDC-2016 separately, and TTTD is the standard literature baseline; both were missing from the candidate set (exclusion reasons unchanged)

candidate_set.description: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) via RustCrypto sha2 =0.11.0, as implemented for every digest and bound as algorithm id 1
SHA-512/256 (FIPS 180-4): faster on 64-bit CPUs, same standard family, length-extension resistant
BLAKE2b-256 (RFC 7693): fast in software on 64-bit CPUs without SHA extensions; the Borg incumbent's chunk-ID hash; no tree mode in the RFC profile
BLAKE3 (C2SP BLAKE3 v1.0.0): tree-native, SIMD/parallel, not NIST/IETF standardised
SHA3-256 (FIPS 202)
KT128/KT256 (RFC 9861, IRTF informational): tree-capable Keccak variant
Ascon-Hash256/Ascon-CXOF128 (NIST SP 800-232): lightweight, customization strings for domain separation
SHA-256 retained but mandate SHA-NI/ARMv8 crypto-extension paths and parallel per-chunk hashing
SHA-256 for v1 plus a registered second algorithm id reserved for a future format version (no in-version negotiation)

correction_reason: round1 program-code critic: BLAKE2b (RFC 7693), an IETF-published digest used for chunk identifiers by the Borg incumbent, was missing from the candidate set
